summary: The exact candidate fixes the reproducible unconditional pinned-memory failures in LoRA layer offsets and torch_native batch metadata on CPU. It is a correct partial fix, but end-to-end CPU LoRA generation for the reported Intel Xeon AMX/Qwen3-VL deployment remains unverified and the candidate's tiny-Llama request hit a separate RoPE NameError.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: TorchNativeLoRABackend.prepare_lora_batch called Tensor.pin_memory and raised RuntimeError: no pinned memory allocator is available.
Exact candidate regression and adversarial CPU checks: 3 passed, including forced pin allocator failure and independent CPU LoRA numerical reference.
LoRA unit compatibility suite: 82 passed, 6 skipped, 14 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: This independent review did not execute GPU kernels; the issue contract is CPU-only. The host has ROCm 7.2 and torch.cuda.is_available() is true, so it cannot emulate an accelerator-free deployment. Candidate-retained GPU evidence was inspected but not counted as an independent run.

remaining_counterexamples: The candidate's tiny-Llama CPU HTTP request did not generate a response; it failed later in the RoPE path with NameError: apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace.
Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with the user's LoRA adapter was not exercised.
An accelerator-free Intel Xeon AMX environment was unavailable, so that architecture and allocator configuration remain unqualified.
remaining_limitations: Available hardware is AMD ROCm, not Intel Xeon AMX, and Torch reports an available accelerator.
No Qwen3-VL weights or user adapter were available.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture can validate transport/engine execution only and the candidate's retained run failed before completing generation.
No native source changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
